definition.name: code-review
definition.description: Review the current branch before it is pushed: three parallel read-only reviewers (correctness, security, tests) over origin/<base>..HEAD, one curator that dedupes and keeps the concrete findings, an optional adversarial verification pass, then a fixer that applies the kept findings and commits them (or, in report mode, leaves the findings file for you). Pre-flight picks harness, model and effort for every reviewer, the curator, the verifier and the fixer. A failed reviewer opens a recovery choice before curation. Never pushes.

inputs.name: base
inputs.prompt: Base branch to diff against (empty = the repo's default branch)

inputs.name: mode
inputs.prompt: apply (fix and commit the kept findings) or report (write the findings file only)

inputs.name: plan_path
inputs.prompt: Plan file whose `## Decisions Made` the review must respect (optional)

inputs.name: guidance
inputs.prompt: Standing guidance for the reviewers (optional)

steps.run:
set -eu
raw=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$raw"' EXIT
cat >"$raw" <<'WISE_BASE'
{{base}}
WISE_BASE
base=$(tr -d '\r' <"$raw" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//' | sed 's@^origin/@@' | head -n 1)
if [ -z "$base" ]; then
  base=$(gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name 2>/dev/null || true)
fi
if [ -z "$base" ]; then
  base=$(git symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's@^origin/@@' || true)
fi
base="${base:-main}"
git fetch --quiet origin "$base" 2>/dev/null || true
if ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet "origin/$base" >/dev/null; then
  echo "ERROR: origin/$base does not exist; pass the base branch as the 'base' input." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "$base"

set -eu
git rev-list --count "origin/{{base}}..HEAD"

steps.run:
set -eu
python3 - "{{run.dir}}" <<'WISE_REVIEW_HEALTH'
import json
import pathlib
import sys

run_dir = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
state = json.loads((run_dir / "state.json").read_text())
unhealthy = []
for lens in ("correctness", "security", "tests"):
    step = state["steps"].get(f"review-{lens}", {})
    report = run_dir / "review" / f"{lens}.md"
    if step.get("status") == "failed" or not report.is_file():

Merge the three reviewer reports for the branch in
{{project.path}} (`origin/{{base}}..HEAD`) into one findings list.

`N. file:line - problem - concrete fix - severity (critical|warning|info)`.
Write the file even when it is empty.

steps.description: Adversarial verification of every kept finding
steps.prompt:
Adversarially verify the findings in `{{findings_path}}` for the
branch in {{project.path}} (`origin/{{base}}..HEAD`). For every
numbered finding, try to REFUTE it against the current code: is it
actually wrong as claimed, on the lines it names, in the way it
describes? Where you have subagents, run one read-only subagent per
finding in parallel; otherwise check them one after another.
Default to refuted when the evidence is ambiguous.

Report only: never edit the worktree, never run a git write
command, never commit.

Overwrite `{{findings_path}}` with only the findings that survive,
renumbered from 1 in the same line format. Write the file even when
nothing survives.

Return the fields directly, no wrapping: `kept` (findings that
survived), `refuted` (findings dropped).

Apply the findings in `{{findings_path}}` to the branch in
{{project.path}} (`origin/{{base}}..HEAD`). An empty file means
nothing to apply: return applied 0, skipped 0, committed no.

For each numbered finding apply the concrete fix in place, bounded:
guard the change, do not redesign it, no behaviour changes beyond
the fix, no broad renames, no new dependencies. Skip a finding
when the fix would need any of those or when the code has moved
on; count it as skipped.

When any file changed: run the project's quickest relevant check
(a syntax check, the affected tests, or the linter in read-only
mode); if the tree is broken, revert your edits with
`git checkout -- <files>` and treat every finding as skipped. Then
stage every change (`git add -A`) and commit with one
Conventional Commits subject in the form
`fix(<scope>): apply code-review findings` where <scope> is the
area most of the fixes touch (drop the scope when there is none).
Commit message body: one line per applied finding. Never add a
Co-Authored-By or any AI attribution trailer. Never push, never
amend, never `--no-verify`. One round: never re-review.

Return the fields directly, no wrapping: `applied` (findings
turned into edits), `skipped` (findings left alone),
`committed` (`yes` when a fix commit landed, else `no`).

steps.run: echo "code-review: origin/{{base}}..HEAD commits={{commit_count}} findings={{findings}} kept={{kept}} refuted={{refuted}} applied={{applied}} skipped={{skipped}} committed={{committed}} file={{findings_path}}" | sed -E 's/\{\{[a-z_]+\}\}//g'

echo "code-review incomplete: missing reviewer reports: {{missing_reviews}}" >&2
exit 1

definition.name: impl-plan-auto
definition.description: Autonomous plan-file -> PR pipeline. Give it one or more PLAN-*.md files (for example the plans /wise-revise writes into docs/plans/); for each one the engine claims a branch and worktree, re-plans the seed against current HEAD, implements the refreshed plan, converges it through a review / fix loop, pushes, opens a PR, requests the bot reviews, watches CI and the bots, fixes what they raise, and merges once the PR is green and quiet. No prompts after launch. One worktree + branch + PR per plan file; a merged PR loses its worktree and local branch, anything else stays open for a human with the worktree kept for inspection.
definition.author: e1024kb

groups.label: Re-plan phase (architect, re-plans the seed at HEAD)
Review gate (3 lenses: correctness, security, tests)

inputs.name: plans
inputs.prompt: Which plan file(s)? Comma-separated PLAN-*.md paths (docs/plans/PLAN-api-caching.md, docs/plans/PLAN-auth-debt.md). Relative paths resolve against the repo root. No spaces when passed positionally.

inputs.name: guidance
inputs.prompt: Optional guidance for this run: skills or libraries to prefer, guidelines, files to avoid. Blank = none.

steps.run:
set -eu
# An autonomous multi-worktree run starts from a clean base.
if ! git diff --quiet || ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
  echo "ERROR: base repo at $(pwd) has uncommitted changes; stash or commit them, then re-run." >&2
  exit 1
fi
gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: gh is not authenticated; run 'gh auth login'." >&2; exit 1; }
git remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: no 'origin' remote." >&2; exit 1; }
echo "PREFLIGHT: ok"

set -eu
# The value lands in a temp file first: bash 3.2 (macOS) cannot
# parse a heredoc inside $( ) when the text has an odd quote.
raw=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$raw"' EXIT
cat >"$raw" <<'WISE_PLANS'
{{plans}}
WISE_PLANS
list=$(tr ',;' '\n\n' <"$raw" | tr -d '\r' \
  | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//' | awk 'NF && !seen[$0]++')
if [ -z "$list" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: no plan files given." >&2
  exit 1
fi
json="["
sep=""
missing=""
while IFS= read -r item; do
  case "$item" in
    /*) path="$item" ;;
    *)  path="$(pwd)/$item" ;;
  esac
  if [ ! -f "$path" ]; then
    missing="$missing $item"
    continue
  fi
  path="$(cd "$(dirname "$path")" && pwd)/$(basename "$path")"
  case "$path" in
    *[\"\\]*|*[[:cntrl:]]*)
      echo "ERROR: plan path '$path' contains a quote, backslash or control character." >&2

`{{run.dir}}/research/audit.md` (skip any that is missing). Where
the design / technical / requirements signals are thin, supplement
with your own Read / Grep of `{{project.path}}` before scoring a
dimension UNKNOWN. Score the ten dimensions, print the scorecard
table, and reach the READY / GAPS verdict. Also write the
scorecard to `{{run.dir}}/research/gap-scorecard.md` so
`build-plan` can read it.

If the verdict is GAPS: read
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/grill/blueprint-format.md and
write `{{run.dir}}/plans/BLUEPRINT-<ref>.md` (mkdir -p the
directory first; <ref> is {{ticket_ref}} with any leading '#'
stripped) exactly to that schema. The user's pre-flight gap mode
is `{{gap_mode}}`: when it is `ask`, ALSO print the per-person
question blocks in your response (they are paste-ready for Slack
/ a ticket comment, and the next step lets the user answer any of
them directly). When it is `defaults` (nobody will answer
mid-run), do NOT paste the blocks; print only the blueprint path
and the per-person question counts. The blocks live in the
BLUEPRINT file either way.

Return the fields directly as the structured result (no wrapping,
no JSON-in-a-string): `readiness` = `ready` or `gaps`,
`open_questions` = the open-question count.

steps.message:
The gap analysis found open questions; the full per-person
blocks are in the blueprint at {{run.dir}}/plans/ (the
BLUEPRINT-<ref>.md file; also printed in the step result above).
Answer the ones you can right here, free text, in any form.
Whatever you leave open proceeds on the stated default, recorded
as an assumption in the plan. If you'd rather take the questions
to your team first: cancel the run now and
/wise-workflow-resume it once you have answers.

steps.prompt:
Act as the wise `architect` role leading a cross-functional
planning pass and cover the `product-manager` (scope /
requirement clarifications), `software-engineer` (reuse vs
extend vs build-new, grounded in the audit), and `qa-engineer`
(testing scope) lenses yourself (see
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/agents/architect.md,
product-manager.md, software-engineer.md, qa-engineer.md).

Consolidate the research into a single investigation. The
evidence lives in files under `{{run.dir}}/research/` (the
steps that wrote them ran as isolated children; you cannot see
their output): the normalised ticket at `{{ticket_path}}`, the
design spec `design.md`, the related items `related.md`, the
Context Dossier `dossier.md`, the codebase audit `audit.md`, and
the gap scorecard `gap-scorecard.md`. Read each one that exists
and skip silently any that is missing (its stage may have been
deselected at pre-flight or produced nothing). Then decide,
AUTONOMOUSLY, with a one-line rationale each, every decision the
work needs: scope & requirement clarifications (product lens),
technical approach (reuse vs extend vs build-new for each
functional piece, grounded in the audit), component & file
choices, design-spec decisions (frontend / fullstack with designs
only), and testing scope (QA lens). Do NOT ask the user anything
here; this is the autonomous consolidated decision the user
reviews next.

Gap handling: the user's answers from `resolve-gaps` are between
the markers below. The block may be empty or hold only the text
`Proceed on the stated defaults` (the user skipped; every
question proceeds on its default), or may contain a raw
un-rendered placeholder token in double curly braces (the gap
verdict was `ready` so the ask step never ran, or the whole gap
stage was deselected at pre-flight); in both cases there is
nothing to fold in. When the gap-analysis stage itself was
deselected, there is no scorecard either: consolidate the
evidence that exists and record the thinner footing under
`## Assumptions`.

---
{{gap_answers}}
---

Treat each answer as CLEAR evidence for its dimension. Every
question left unanswered proceeds on its stated default, recorded
verbatim in `## Assumptions` and flagged `default-accepted`. If a
`BLUEPRINT-<ref>.md` exists in `{{run.dir}}/plans/`, write the
answers back into it (Answer lines + Clarifications log, per
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/grill/blueprint-format.md) and
flip its status line to `RESOLVED -> see PLAN-<ref>.md`.

Write the plan to a file. First ensure the directory exists, then
write with the `Write` tool:

  mkdir -p "{{run.dir}}/plans"
  # file: {{run.dir}}/plans/PLAN-<ref>.md
  # where <ref> is {{ticket_ref}} with any leading '#' stripped
  # (e.g. PLAN-PROJ-777.md, PLAN-678.md)

Plan structure:

  # {{tracker_slug}}:{{ticket_ref}} - <Title>
  ## Summary
  ## Assumptions
  ## Decisions Made     (each decision + one-line rationale)
  ## Design Notes       (per-component layout / states; include
    only for a frontend / fullstack ticket with designs)
  ## Tasks              (grouped into parallelizable WAVES; each
    task notes "Reuse: ..." or "New: ..." with file paths, and a
    per-task SP; include the summed total SP)
  ## Testing
  ## Validation         (type-check / lint / tests checklist; add a
    visual-match item for a frontend ticket with designs)

For SP estimation consult the `wise-estimation` reference skill
(Fibonacci scale; scope / complexity / uncertainty axes;
decompose so every task <= 3 SP; round the summed total to the
nearest Fibonacci).

Return the field directly as the structured result (no wrapping,
no JSON-in-a-string): `plan_path` = the absolute path you wrote.

Read the plan at `{{plan_path}}` and present it to the user for
review; informational only, no decisions, no questions. Show:

  Plan file: {{plan_path}}

then, rendered from the file, the **## Summary**, **## Design
Notes** (skip if absent), **## Decisions Made**, **## Testing**,
and **## Validation** sections. The user's pre-flight review mode
is `{{review_mode}}`: if it is `ask`, tell them they can comment
to adjust the plan in the next step or accept it as-is; if it is
`auto`, note the plan is accepted as presented and can be
adjusted later by editing the file or re-running.

steps.message:
You've reviewed the plan at {{plan_path}}. Any comments or
adjustments before we set up the branch? For example: a decision
to change, a missed constraint, libraries to avoid, files to stay
out of, or extra acceptance criteria. Accept as-is to keep the
plan unchanged.

steps.when: review_mode == 'ask' && user_comments != '' && user_comments != 'Accept the plan as-is'
steps.prompt:
Act as the wise `architect` role (see
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/agents/architect.md).

The user reviewed the plan at `{{plan_path}}` and asked for
changes:

---
{{user_comments}}
---

Re-read the plan, fold these comments in (adjust the affected
Decisions / Tasks / Testing / Validation sections), and OVERWRITE
`{{plan_path}}` with the revised plan: same section structure,
same heading. Then give the user a 2-4 line summary of what
changed. One revision pass only.

The plan is settled. Act on the pre-flight SETUP choices; ask the
user (through the `wise_ask` tool) ONLY about the pieces they
left on `ask`. The modes:

  branch_mode:    {{branch_mode}}     (auto | current | ask)
  implement_mode: {{implement_mode}}  (plan-only | now | ask)

First compute the target branch from `{{ticket_ref}}` per
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/branch-naming.md`; the branch is
the ticket ref EXACTLY, no prefix:
  - acronym ref (^[A-Za-z]+-\d+$, e.g. PROJ-777) -> use verbatim;
  - bare number (^#?\d+$, e.g. #678) -> `abstract-task-<digits>`;
  - never add ticket/ jira/ linear/ feat/ wise/ or any `/`.
Call this `target_branch`. The branch at run start was
`{{current_branch}}`; re-read the current branch with
`git -C "{{project.path}}" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`.

The ticket ref is IMMUTABLE here: the plan file, its heading, and
target_branch all derive from `{{ticket_ref}}`, so setup never
offers to change it. If the extracted ref is wrong, stop with a
clear message; the fix is a fresh run from ticket fetch, not a
rename at setup.

Resolve each piece from its mode. Any branch switch or creation
FIRST refuses a dirty tree (`git diff --quiet && git diff
--cached --quiet` in `{{project.path}}`; if dirty, tell the user
to stash/commit and `/wise-workflow-resume <run-ulid>`, then
stop without the structured result so the step fails and can be
resumed). Carrying uncommitted changes across a checkout is never
acceptable, existing branch or new.

- Branch: `auto`: if the current branch already equals
  target_branch, nothing to do; else if target_branch exists,
  dirty-check then `git checkout <target_branch>`; else
  dirty-check, resolve the repo's default branch
  (`git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, falling
  back to `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef`), and create the
  branch FROM it: `git checkout -b <target_branch>
  origin/<default>`, never from whatever branch happens to be
  checked out.
  `current`: do nothing; stay on the current branch.
  `ask`: ask the user with `wise_ask` (ONLY if the current branch
  != target_branch; when they already match, do not ask): options
  `Create <target_branch>` / `Switch to existing <target_branch>`
  (offer only if that branch already exists) / `Stay on <current
  branch>`. When the answer is Create, ask a second `wise_ask` for
  the base branch: the repo's default branch first, then recent
  `release*` branches; free text allowed. Then act exactly as the
  `auto` rules describe (dirty-tree refusal before every checkout;
  the branch name MUST equal target_branch exactly).
- Implement: `now`: implement_choice=yes. `plan-only`:
  implement_choice=no. `ask`: ask the user with `wise_ask`
  ("Implement the plan now?", options `Yes, implement now` /
  `No, plan only`).

Do not rename the session here; the harness owns session naming.

Return the fields directly as the structured result (no wrapping,
no JSON-in-a-string): `work_branch` = the branch now checked out,
`implement_choice` = `yes` or `no`.

The user chose to implement the plan now. Read
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/workflows/ticket-auto/prompts/implement-plan.md
and follow it end to end on the current branch {{work_branch}},
with:
  plan_path:    {{plan_path}}
  worktree:     {{project.path}}
  project.kind: {{project.kind}}
The plan's task waves are phase gates: dispatch each wave's tasks
to parallel fresh-context executor `Task` subagents, then simplify
+ commit each task serially (one atomic commit per task). Never
push; the user opens the PR separately.

Return the fields directly as the structured result (no wrapping,
no JSON-in-a-string): `impl_waves`, `impl_tasks`, `impl_done`,
`impl_failed` (integers).

Print the closing summary. Link the ticket only with the `url`
from the run context `ticket` entry (`wise_context` key
`ticket`); never invent a tracker URL.

  Ticket:  {{tracker_slug}}:{{ticket_ref}}
  Branch:  {{work_branch}}
  Plan:    {{plan_path}}

Then branch on the implement decision (`{{implement_choice}}`,
resolved by `setup` from the pre-flight `implement_mode`, or from
the user's answer when that mode was `ask`):

  - If it is `yes`: implementation already ran in the previous
    step; its tallies are waves={{impl_waves}}
    tasks={{impl_tasks}} done={{impl_done}}
    failed={{impl_failed}}. Confirm the work landed as per-task
    commits on `{{work_branch}}` (nothing pushed), then point at
    the natural next steps:
      - Review the branch:  /wise-workflow-run code-review
        (three reviewers, a curator, an optional verifier and a
        fixer; harness, model and effort per agent at pre-flight)
      - Open a PR:          /wise-pr-create
    If any task came back `failed`, tell the user to inspect those
    commits before reviewing.

  - Otherwise (the user skipped): tell the user their options:
      - Implement now:  /wise-implement-plan-auto {{plan_path}}
      - Save for later: the plan file persists in the run
        directory; resume this session from /resume's picker.
    For 3+ parallel tasks in a single wave, mention that
    `/wise-implement-plan-auto` runs each wave's tasks in parallel.

Suggest `/rename {{ticket_ref}}_ticket-plan` as a command the
user can run to label this session for /resume's picker.
